analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump plus a new paragraph on SSD victim selection around head lines 531-546) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (date bump plus a new "Active-store victim selection" row near line 372). No executable code, keys, crypto, protocol or authorization behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. The prose describes an eviction-selection implementation in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot, which is not supplied. I could not verify those source changes, only the docs.

Relevant threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache, at-rest artifact, TTL/LRU bounds). The documented behavior leaves intact the 30-minute sliding TTL, the box-wide LRU disk budget, file leases, epoch validation and the removal lock. It says concurrent schedules may pick different victims from a snapshot taken before the first attempt. That affects eviction ordering only, not confidentiality. The TTL and disk-budget guarantees are enforced by separate maintenance paths (SSDWholeRootMaintainer, documented in the same table) and are not weakened by what the docs say. The "external-removal reconciliation stops the pass so the budget can recheck usage" note is a small availability and disk-budget nuance; the maintenance sweep runs every 60s, so I see no TTL or budget regression in the docs.

The visible context portion of prefix-cache.md (lines 858-969) reads as unchanged documentation. It contains no new claims on encryption, routing scope or attestation, and invariants and code-map entries are consistent with existing text. Remaining question for integration: whether the actual code change to eviction (not in this batch) preserves unlink-and-index-removal semantics, the TTL expiry and the epoch-rotation rules from T-041. The threat model does not need an update from these docs alone.
